ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory ex-ante screening of all incorporators, directors, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Spanish BOE/SEPBLAC precautionary measures, and OFAC SDN List; PEP determination for Spanish and foreign politically exposed persons under art. 4.2 of Ley 10/2010; screening evidence and KYC files retained for at least ten years under art. 25 of Ley 10/2010; enhanced due diligence triggered by any sanctions hit, PEP status, or opacity in the ownership chain.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - Sede Electrónica (https://www.rmc.es); negative name certificate application via the RMC electronic certification service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Denominations must be expressed in Spanish or a co-official Spanish language (Catalan/Valencian, Basque, Galician) using Latin script; foreign-root words are admitted only in Latin transliteration and must respect Spanish orthographic conventions; the denomination must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing company name; the corporate form suffix 'S.L.' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' is mandatory and is not part of the distinctive denomination
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed denomination, the applicant may, within one month of notification, file a written reconsideration request with the Registro Mercantil Central; an adverse determination may be appealed administratively (recurso de alzada) to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice, with judicial recourse before the Juzgado Central de lo Contencioso-Administrativo within two months; in parallel, the applicant may file a fresh application proposing up to three alternative denominations. No statutory extension of the 90-day name reservation is available after expiry; a new negative certificate application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual mailbox is not permissible as the sole statutory seat (domicilio social) of an SL: the incorporation deed must state a real registered address within Spain. A shared professional office address may be tolerated administratively, but the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) may challenge artificial domiciles. For ISIC 4390 deep foundation and diaphragm wall contracting, the company must also hold an operational seat, equipment depot, contractor accreditation, and occupational-safety registration (Registro de Empresas Acreditadas - REA) in the relevant autonomous community, rendering a virtual-only structure commercially and regulatory unacceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Annual probability of unannounced AEAT/SEPLAC inspection of the registered office is estimated at 10-15% for a low-risk standard contractor; unannounced labour and occupational-safety inspections of active construction worksites in ISIC 4390 exceed 75% per year under national construction-site inspection programs; municipal licensing verification is conducted at registration and on commencement of activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (Articles 1-50 covering incorporation formalities, share capital, board governance and corporate acts)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrato de constitución de la sociedad de responsabilidad limitada
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of 3,000 euros fully paid in cash or assets upon incorporation; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

Upon incorporation, the Board of Directors of the Company, a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, hereby resolves unanimously:

1. To approve the subscription by the promoters of the entire share capital amounting to three thousand euros (3,000 EUR) as evidenced by the share certificates.
2. To establish and adopt the registered office at [Address], 28001 Madrid, Spain, as the principal place of business.
3. To appoint Mr. John Doe, Ms. Jane Smith, and Mr. Robert Brown as the Directors of the Company and Ms. Emily Davis as the Secretary of the Board.
4. To authorize the immediate opening of bank accounts and the performance of all acts necessary for the proper administration of the Company.
5. To ratify all actions taken by the promoters prior to incorporation.

This resolution was adopted on [Date] at the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Incorporation Contract and Statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario Público) through the official Spanish Notary Registry portal or local notary office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the 'Contrato de constitución' and 'Estatutos Sociales' in Spanish. Submit the documents to a notary for review and execution. The notary will authenticate the signatures and issue the public deed of incorporation. Pay the notary fees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request amendment of documents within the statutory period if corrections are needed

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Documents with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central via the online portal at www.registradores.org or e-Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized 'Contrato de constitución' and 'Estatutos' along with the certificate issued by the notary. Pay the registry filing fee. Obtain the registration certificate, CIF (NIF), and inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an appeal or request rectification if the application is rejected or queried by the registry

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or Simplified Declaration for small-scale construction works
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with air quality, noise, and waste disposal standards under Spanish environmental regulations (Royal Decree 105/2021)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire brigade (Bomberos), structural safety inspections, and compliance with workplace health and safety standards (ITSS)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL companies obtain NIF (CIF) upon registration with the Commercial Registry. Foreign entities establishing presence in Spain must apply to the Tax Agency for NIF issuance with supporting documents including incorporation deed, proof of address, and business activity description.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No elective check-the-box regimes; standard SL entities are taxed at corporate level under the general tax regime. Limited hybrid mismatch election options may apply under EU ATAD rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturación electrónica for VAT taxpayers; real-time fiscal information reporting to AEAT via digital platforms; electronic clearance and digital stamping required for transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for 0% VAT rate upon proof of export outside the EU. Services zero-rated if performed outside Spain or to non-residents under specific conditions.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of fraudulent zero-rating result in tax reassessment, penalties up to 100% of evaded VAT, interest surcharges, and potential criminal prosecution with clawback of benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the European System of Central Banks and under the prudential and supervisory framework of the European Central Bank; foreign exchange administration is also governed by the Spanish Ministry of Economy and Competitiveness and the General Directorate of International Trade and Investments, with the Banco de España as the designated monitoring and statistical reporting institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is part of the euro area and maintains full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions, subject only to European Union treaty freedoms and limited safeguards. Profit remittance by a Spanish Sociedad de Limitada to non-resident shareholders is freely permitted without prior administrative authorization, provided that the distributable reserves are duly audited and stated in legally approved annual financial statements, that corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) has been settled, and that the statutory legal reserve requirements under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital are complied with. There are no exchange controls on the euro, but reporting obligations arise under Royal Decree 505/1985 for direct foreign investment, foreign borrowing, and payments/receipts with non-resident persons; no convertibility restriction applies to the euro, and the free movement of capital applies vis-à-vis other EU members, with certain verification and statistical declaration requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain maintains no general statutory requirement for export proceeds to be surrendered to the central bank or to be mandatorily converted into euros. Exporters invoicing in foreign currency may retain the foreign exchange proceeds in accounts held with Spanish credit institutions or EU-authorized financial institutions. However, proceeds must be reported to the Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistical purposes within the applicable deadlines under Order EHA/3015/2006 and related implementing regulations, typically through the integrated reporting system of the Banco de España using form R-02 for operations exceeding €12,500 or the equivalent. If an account with a non-resident financial institution is opened or maintained, prior filing with the Banco de España's Declaración de Posiciones y Operaciones en el Exterior may be required on an annual basis. There is no compulsory conversion ratio or mandatory repatriation ratio for export receipts in Spain.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions, whether Spanish-authorised entities supervised by the Banco de España or EU-authorised passporting into Spain under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), may be used for receiving milestone payments and trade-related disbursements as secondary liquidity rails. However, principal operating or escrow accounts for material international infrastructure projects should remain at full-service credit institutions due to the need for SWIFT correspondent banking, robust KYC/KYB during the statutory license-related project windows, issuance of bank guarantees and standby LCs, and integration with project finance consent agreements. Offshore digital EMIs not established in the EEA face significant legal constraints because cross-border payment services into Spain require authorisation or passporting under PSD2, and passporting from non-EEA jurisdictions is generally not available; unlicensed or non-passported foreign EMIs cannot lawfully provide payment accounts or execute transactions with Spanish resident merchants in a business capacity. The use of an unauthorised third-country EMI may additionally trigger AML/CFT risk under Law 10/2010 and impede the capacity to obtain corporate banking underwriting facilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish anti-money laundering regulations (Law 10/2010, as amended by Royal Decree 304/2014 and EU Directives) establish a general principle of due diligence requiring the credit institution to know the identity of the beneficial owner and to verify the identity of the legal entity's ultimate beneficial owners. For a Spanish risk tier of 'Low_Risk_Standard' (undertaking works under ISIC 4390, deep foundation and diaphragm wall construction), onboarding may in certain banks be completed remotely using electronic identification and qualified digital signatures, including the DNIe, certificate-based e-signatures, or a Spain-based representation with notarised powers of attorney. However, in practice, the senior director or a duly empowered attorney-in-fact with a notarised and apostilled power of attorney must hold an in-person or video-identity interview with the bank's compliance officer, particularly where the account will receive foreign capital contributions and disburse international trade settlements. The AML preventive measures for enhanced due diligence always apply if any director resides outside the EU, but no universal statutory mandate exists that every director must physically appear; a single authorised signatory appearing either physically or via an accredited video call, supported by certified corporate documents and legalisation from the Spanish Consulate or Apostille, normally satisfies the KYC interview. The onboarding standard for project-based treasury accounts can nevertheless require the beneficial owner and the appointed operations director to appear on site at a Spanish branch due to internal underwriting policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or opaque ownership structure: foreign holding company or ultimate beneficial owner resident in a non-EU tax haven jurisdiction triggers enhanced due diligence under Law 10/2010 and Article 3 of the Spanish AML regulation on beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully certified copy of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada's public deed of incorporation and articles of association; current certificate of the beneficial ownership registry (Registro de Titularidades Reales) or equivalent notarised declaration of beneficial owners; audited financial statements or interim balance sheet; CV and passport copies of all directors; proof of residential and tax residency address for each UB; corporate chart or organigramme demonstrating a clear economic nexus; and a written business plan outlining the ISIC 4390 geotechnical project, source of funds, counterparties, and projected account transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International capital injection from non-EU jurisdiction with ambiguous origin-of-funds documentation and no clear client contractual counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share capital contribution agreement or capital loan agreement; SWIFT MT103 payment notification and bank reference from the remitting bank; certified source of wealth statement (e.g., audited financial statements, tax returns, inheritance documentation, or sale-and-purchase agreements that generated the funds); a project finance or binding works contract with the downstream client referencing the specific deep diaphragm wall project site in Spain; and a legal opinion from a qualified counsel confirming that the funding transaction is not disguised money laundering or an irregular capital movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade disbursements to related parties or sub-contractors without verifiable underlying geotechnical works, generating vendor-payment red flags during the statutory works registration procedure requiring proof of real economic activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original sub-contracts and commercial invoices; certificates of execution and progress reports (e.g., daily reports, concrete pour sheets, slurry wall quantity surveys); site access records or geotechnical engineer's valuations; signed purchase orders for bentonite, drilling equipment, or rebar cages; and copies of the contractor license and ISO 9001/14001 certifications, if any, to evidence operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Milestone payments routed through correspondent banks in multiple jurisdictions creating fragmented transaction trails before crediting to the Spanish account, triggering suspicion under Article 17 of Law 10/2010 on unusual or complex transfer patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master milestone payment schedule in the head contract; bank account statements covering the full transaction path from the client to the Spanish operating account; legal explanation of the financing structure (e.g., interposed special-purpose vehicle, escrow or trustee arrangement); notarised power of attorney for the project finance administrator; and all signed side letters or disbursement conditions relating to the milestone release.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injections into the Spanish SL account should be executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the non-resident investor's bank account to the SL's euro-denominated operating or escrow account maintained at a Spanish credit institution. The remittance must be labelled with the appropriate ISO 20022 purpose code, typically 'CAPT' for contribution to the company capital or 'CBLK' for blocked/escrow funds, with the narrative referencing the corporate deed and capital increase or equity injection. Spain maintains a statistical-declarative regime rather than a prior authorisation regime: direct foreign investment exceeding €3,000,000 million or originating from countries on certain tax-haven lists must be declared to the Registro de Inversiones (Investment Registry) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy after the operation is carried out, using the post-investment Form D-1A and annual Form D-2 for updates. For capital injections relating to the ISIC 4390 diaphragm wall project, the routing must also ensure that the receiving bank can verify the underlying contract and source of funds to mitigate AML/JMLSG concerns, and the bank should be supplied with the executed corporate deed, notarial certification, an resolution of the sole shareholder or board approving the share premium or capital increase, and the Qualified Electronic Signature identification for the authorising director.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for cross-border geotechnical works and procurement should be settled over standard correspondent banking rails using SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for direct payments to third-party suppliers or sub-contractors, and globally accepted letter of credit mechanisms, primarily irrevocable, confirmed letters of credit issued by Spanish or EU banks in favour of foreign equipment suppliers, with the compliant terms set under UCP 600, ICC Publication No. 600. For payment under a commercial letter of credit, the Spanish importer should request, or if acting as exporter use, the documentary package: commercial invoice, packing list, full set of bill of lading or international consignment note (CMR for road, CIM for rail, or AWB for air freight), certificate of origin (form EUR.1 or the exporter's statement per Regulation (EU) No. 952/2013 depending on preferential origin), insurance certificate, inspection certificate for geotechnical machinery, and any balance-of-payments reporting code in the underlying remittance instruction. Transactions exceeding €12,500 must be included in the bank's balance-of-payments reporting to the Banco de España, and the guidelines of Circular 1/2023 of the Banco de España on balance-of-payments statistics apply. Payments to EU counterparties are unrestricted; payments to non-EU countries are likewise unrestricted unless the counterparty is subject to EU financial sanctions or restrictive measures under Regulation (EC) 2580/2001, Regulation (EU) 833/2014 (Russia-related measures), or the relevant Common Foreign and Security Policy decisions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards between EUR and USD, GBP, or construction-procurement currencies (e.g., Turkish lira, Egyptian pound, or Middle Eastern currencies) entered into with a Spanish or EU-authorized investment firm or credit institution, evidenced by an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a local FX master agreement, provided that the transaction is permissible under the Spanish securities market regulations and does not create a speculative position triggering additional margin and reporting duties.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing other currencies for currencies not freely deliverable in the euro area, subject to the counterparty being an EU-authorized institution and the transaction being documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex; profit remittance hedging can use NDFs to fix the euro-equivalent value of foreign-denominated milestone receipts in illiquid emerging-market currencies.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) for financing liquidity projections involving a non-EU project SPV and euro-denominated cash flows, documented under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, with the settlement through continuous linked settlement or standard Clearing House Interbank Payments System procedures, and subject to EMIR clearing or risk mitigation obligations if the counterparty is a non-financial counterparty exceeding the clearing threshold.

FX options (European style, vanilla or knock-in barrier) for a zero-cost collar hedging the beneficiary's downside on foreign-currency export receipts, using premium payment in EUR, with the underlying tenor aligned to the project implementation schedule of the diaphragm wall works and with the transaction reported to the Banco de España for statistical purposes when the notional exceeds the reporting threshold.

FX swaps involving spot euro conversion with a simultaneous forward re-conversion, deployed solely to phase project liquidity without speculative intent, compliant with the business purpose and Treasury policy of the Spanish SL and recorded in the annual financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) deposit — balance sheet, profit-and-loss, statement of changes in equity, notes, management report and attached UBO beneficial-ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office; coordinated via the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by shareholders within six months of the financial year-end and deposit within one month of approval. For a 31 December year-end: general meeting no later than 30 June and registry deposit no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Closure of the commercial registry for the company ('cierre registral'), preventing any subsequent corporate filing until the accounts are properly deposited; administrative monetary sanctions may be imposed, and prolonged non-deposit exposes directors to company-debt liability and possible judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades — Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the expiration of six months after the close of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the filing deadline is 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating surcharge for late self-assessment and punitive late-interest; fixed penalties for omitted, incorrect or false data; possible indirect estimation (estimación indirecta) by AEAT and seizure proceedings in the case of persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT recapulative return (Modelo 390) — annual summary of VAT declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 January following the close of the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or deficient filing triggers fines under the General Tax Law (typically EUR 150–600), default interest on VAT due, and potential surcharge for late payment; repeated non-filing may lead to quarterly penalties and forced assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory for an SL that, for two consecutive financial years, meets two of the following thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total assets greater than EUR 2,840,000; annual turnover greater than EUR 5,700,000; average permanent headcount greater than 50. Audit is also required for listed entities, financial-sector/regulated or consolidated subsidiaries, and where a shareholder or the court applies a statutory audit request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) as adopted by the Instituto de Contabilidad y Auditoria de Cuentas (ICAC), in line with EU Accounting Directive; listed consolidated groups apply EU-endorsed IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO confirmation exists for an SL; the UBO declaration is submitted together with the annual accounts deposit to the Mercantile Registry. The UBO declaration must reflect any shareholding transfers occurring during the year and must be updated before the registry will accept the annual deposit. The confirmation point is therefore the annual accounts filing deadline (by 31 July for a calendar-year SL).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–800 per annum for a professional registered office/registered agent service in Spain.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–7,500 per audit for an independent certified audit of a mid-sized construction contractor, subject to company size and project activity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); 15% reduced rate for newly created Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada during the first two tax periods in which they obtain a positive tax base, provided they carry on an economic activity and are not classified as a passive holding entity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% new-entity rate; R&D and technological innovation credits (30-50%); reinvestment of extraordinary income exemption; deductions for international double taxation relief; for business scope ISIC 4390, possible employer hiring subsidies and regional construction investment credits; no general notional interest deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward for tax losses (bases imponibles negativas) generated from 1 January 2015; however, annual offset is capped at 60% of the tax base for taxpayers with net turnover of EUR 20-60 million and 25% for taxpayers with net turnover exceeding EUR 60 million; no cap applies for taxpayers with net turnover below EUR 20 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (annual Corporate Income Tax return / Impuesto sobre Sociedades), filed mandatorily via the AEAT electronic registration system (Sede Electrónica de la AEAT); quarterly advance payments filed via Modelo 202 (or Modelo 202S for companies in group taxation).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return (Modelo 200) plus three quarterly estimated tax instalments (pagos fraccionados) using Modelo 202.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year entities, the deadline is 1-25 July of the year following the close of the fiscal year (e.g., for FY 2025, due 25 July 2026). Quarterly instalments are due 1-20 April, October, and December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before tax recorded in the statutory financial statements prepared under Spanish GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the profit after reconciliation from the parent-company books to Spanish GAAP; no translation of the global group result may appear here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments to accounting profit (e.g., disallowed expenses, tax-exempt income, timing differences).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back disclaimed costs such as non-documented related-party management fees, penalties, and gifts; subtract exempt dividends from subsidiaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 00500-Base imponible antes de compensación de bases imponibles negativas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base after all corrections, before applying tax-loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure every intercompany invoice has a supporting economic-substance file if controlled; otherwise AEAT will disallow the adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 00504-Base imponible del período (después de compensación)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after offset of prior years' negative tax bases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the offset caps mentioned in the corporate tax regime; for foreign-owned SL, ensure the tax-loss history is traceable and not a cross-border loss-transfer device.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability computed by applying the statutory 25% rate (or 15% for qualifying new entities) to the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced 15% rate is not available if the entity was previously dormant for tax purposes or lacks the effective economic activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Liquid tax after application of credits, double-taxation relief, and withholding; final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach all Modelo 202 instalments paid; any excess withholding on foreign-sourced revenue must be claimed through the corresponding refund procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing recharges: 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6 months), 15% (within 12 months), or 20% (after 12 months) plus late-payment interest; non-filing within the voluntary period exposes the taxpayer to a flat penalty under Article 193 LGT ranging from EUR 200 (no tax due) to 5%-20% of the tax not paid; failure to file correct data may trigger penalties of EUR 300-3,000 per item of data.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (domestic statutory withholding, applicable to residents of EU/EEA jurisdictions and states with a double tax convention); 24% for residents of countries with no DTA and not EU/EEA; 19% for capital gains on disposal of shares was unified as well; 5%-15% or 0% under the applicable DTA, depending on ownership share and treaty terms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty counterparty's tax authority, covering the year of income; before or at the time of the dividend distribution, the withholding agent must fill out and file Modelo 290 for the reduced rate if the treaty provides for a lower domestic withholding rate; if the standard 19%/24% has been withheld, the non-resident recipient may apply for refund via Modelo 210 (Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes) within the four-year statutory limitation period; the AEAT will verify the entitlement through the beneficial-ownership clause and the OECD BEPS minimum standard.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest and royalties to non-resident companies without a permanent establishment are generally subject to Non-Resident Income Tax at 19% for residents of EU/EEA or DTA countries and 24% for other non-residents; under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC), a 0% withholding is available for qualifying EU parent-subsidiary and sister-company payments (25% minimum direct shareholding for two years); typical DTA rates: interest 0%-15% (often 10%), royalties 0%-10%, with additional beneficial-ownership and substance verification requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared if the Spanish entity's net turnover in the preceding tax year exceeded EUR 10,000,000 OR its aggregate related-party transactions exceeded EUR 100,000 per year; Master File must be prepared if the Spanish entity belongs to a multinational group whose consolidated annual revenue exceeds EUR 10,000,000; documentation must be submitted electronically to AEAT in a contemporaneous manner and in Spanish or a language accepted by the AEAT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a self-standing formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime analogous to BVI or the Crown Dependencies. However, substance is tested through the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 15 LGT), the ATAD transposition CFC rules (Chapter IX of Law 27/2014), and treaty shopping provisions (MLI). For an ISIC 4390 deep foundation contractor, economic substance is demonstrated by physical offices, permanent local staff/engineers, production equipment, project management, local bank accounts, and actual construction activities in Spain. If the SL is merely an empty shell interposed to claim treaty benefits or avoid taxable presence, the AEAT may recharacterize the structure, deny treaty benefits, and impose 35%-50% penalties on the adjusted amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting invoicing for completed geotechnical contracts, inflating subcontractor costs without substantiation, booking private expenses as construction costs, or maintaining undisclosed foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax settlement plus late interest; administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the evaded tax (Article 191 LGT); if the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, the conduct constitutes a criminal tax offence under Spanish Criminal Code Article 305, carrying imprisonment of 2-6 years, fines up to six times the evaded amount, and loss of grants or tax benefits for a period of 3-6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives may be jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax debts under Article 42.1 LGT if they intentionally caused or participated in the evasion; in criminal cases, the court may impose travel bans, seizure of personal assets, corporate dissolution, and disqualification from managing corporations for 3-10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Structuring / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining an SL with no operational substance while channelling deep-foundation contract revenue through the entity purely to access Spanish DTA benefits or to shift profits to a low-tax jurisdiction; failure to comply with the minimum economic activity test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under Article 15 LGT (conflict in the application of the tax rule) results in re-assessment at 25% CIT plus interest; penalty of 35%-50% (Articles 110-170 LGT) on the reassessed base; denial of treaty relief; potential application of the CFC rules to attribute passive income to the Spanish parent or foreign shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If civil veil-piercing is applied under Spanish tort law (levantamiento del velo), directors may be personally ordered to pay corporate tax arrears; in an EU-level anti-avoidance context, directors could face criminal charges for money laundering if the shell is used to disguise the beneficial owner, with attendant travel bans and imprisonment up to 6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., equipment rental, subcontracting, central procurement or management fees) at non-arm's-length prices; failing to compile, maintain, or file Local File and Master File above the applicable thresholds; not filing the annual TP disclosure return (Modelo 232).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalties under Article 198.4 LGT: EUR 1,500 per item of omitted or incorrect data, with a minimum of EUR 15,000 for an entirely missing Local File or Master File; separate penalty of 25% of the amount of related-party adjustment if the TP documentation was not maintained; interest from the original due date; potential reassessment of the taxpayer at the higher market value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the non-arm's-length agreements and control the Spanish entity may be declared jointly responsible for the resulting tax debt under Article 42 LGT; if the TP mispricing reaches the criminal threshold (evaded tax > EUR 120,000), personal criminal liability is possible, including imprisonment of 2-6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Beneficial Ownership Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting milestone bank transfers or letters of credit without adequate Customer Due Diligence (CDD) on the ultimate beneficial owner of the foreign contractor; failing to file a suspicious transaction report (STR/SAR) in relation to unusual advances, layered jurisdiction payments, or non-transparent funding of the Spanish SL; failing to register or update the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) records with the Mercantile Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions under Spain's Law 10/2010 on Money Laundering: minor violations EUR 1,000-20,000; serious violations EUR 20,001-60,000; very serious violations EUR 60,001-5,000,000 (or up to three times the amount of the transaction); additionally, unauthorised failure to maintain the UBO registry can lead to a penalty of EUR 3,000-300,000 and delisting from the registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SL are personally liable for their own lack of diligence; if they knowingly facilitated money laundering, Spanish Criminal Code Article 302 applies, with imprisonment of 6-20 years and fines equal to three times the value of the proceeds; travel bans and corporate veil-piercing are common enforcement tools.
